title: Implement secret redaction baseline
verify: Redaction helper masks .env values, tokens, passwords, DB URLs with credentials, and auth material.
Bootstrap and DB scripts use safe output paths and do not print secret material.
Errors/log-like strings used by Foundation tests are redacted.

commands: synthetic secret sample-output check for bootstrap/db scripts
verify.summary: Functional verification passed: targeted redaction tests passed with 9 tests, related Foundation backend tests passed with 24 tests, mb-lint passed across 135 files, git diff --check passed, and synthetic secret-bearing script output checks did not leak secrets. Scope stayed inside task implementation files plus required protocol/evidence artifacts; forbidden production/provider/hosted-auth/product-auth scope was not touched. T3 closure remains pending per-task /red-verify semantic-pass plus human checkpoint and rollback/recovery markers.

Semantic verification passed: implementation fits the Foundation redaction baseline, does not widen into product auth/session, provider setup, hosted identity/recovery, or production secret storage, and does not alter product runtime state or authority boundaries. Residual risk is expected baseline scope: this is pattern-based redaction, not full DLP. T3 closure still requires exact HUMAN_CHECKPOINT and ROLLBACK_RECOVERY_NOTE markers plus explicit closure/sync ownership.

verify.manual_closure_owner: ROLE GENERAL per direct user instruction; user stated human check completed
verify.summary: Closed after /verify PASS and /red-verify semantic-pass. Human checkpoint supplied by user. Rollback/recovery note recorded. Exact T3 closure markers are present in closure protocol and closure report.

constraints: Do not log or export secrets, API keys, tokens, .env values, credentials, or auth material.
Do not weaken local auth/authz assumptions.
Do not invent provider secrets or hosted recovery behavior.
invariants: Secrets/auth material must not enter logs, timeline, manifests, Bus, UI Feed, screenshots, exports, or agent context.
MVP data and artifacts remain local/private by default.
purpose: Provide a security-sensitive redaction baseline for local bootstrap, settings, DB scripts, and future feature evidence.
success_outcome: Future feature tasks can call a shared redaction primitive and Foundation evidence cannot leak auth or secret material.

stop_conditions: A required test or script would print unredacted credentials.
Redaction policy conflicts with API Guidelines or Invariants.
The task requires reading or exposing real secrets.
